sentences.text: Researchers used a mouse model of focal ischemic stroke to investigate the mechanisms behind reduced rehabilitation efficacy.

They identified Lynx1, a protein that modulates nicotinic acetylcholine receptors, as a factor limiting neural plasticity, noting that its levels in neurons surrounding the injury dropped temporarily before returning to normal.

Reducing Lynx1 activity resulted in more clustering of synapses and a higher rate of change in dendritic spines, which improved both natural motor recovery and the effectiveness of rehabilitation during the chronic stage.

A drug targeting Lynx1 given during the chronic phase boosted rehabilitation benefits, suggesting that how dendritic spines change in the area around the stroke is a major factor in how well rehabilitation works.
